headline: High-risk shared-state and write-capable orchestration pair can leak data and cascade errors; prompt-injection risk is lower but present via shared workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write files and uses a per-conversation datastore shared across instances, so attacker-controlled content can bridge into another agent’s context. Prefect’s profile is sparse, but its orchestration role means outputs may be consumed downstream. The pathway is plausible without assuming undocumented channels, so I choose medium over low due to shared state uncertainty.
conditions: IF Dify writes untrusted content into shared datastore or uploaded files
IF Prefect consumes workflow metadata or task outputs from that shared store
mitigations: Separate per-agent workspaces
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages
Require explicit human review before forwarding content
requires-engineering: enforce channel-level content filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge base content, conversation logs, and secrets, while Prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad network egress. A shared datastore or workspace can expose sensitive Dify data to Prefect outputs or logs. The profiles do not prove a default leak, but the shared-state pathway is enough to rate medium.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or datastore
IF Prefect logs or exports workflow metadata containing Dify-originated content
mitigations: Use separate credentials per agent
Store secrets outside shared workspaces
Redact logs before export
Restrict network egress for Prefect jobs
requires-engineering: add data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify has filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and broad egress; Prefect is an orchestration system with broad egress and workflow automation. Even without explicit write permissions for Prefect, overlapping control over mutable workflow state can create conflicts when both operate on the same resources. Uncertainty about Prefect’s write surfaces pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Prefect tasks and Dify workflows target the same files or workflow metadata
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking or optimistic concurrency
mitigations: Assign disjoint resource namespaces
Serialize writes through a single coordinator
Turn on locking for shared artifacts
Limit Dify to read-only access where possible
requires-engineering: implement conflict detection

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can generate workflow outputs from agent/tool runs, and Prefect is an automation/orchestration system that may act on workflow metadata. If Prefect treats Dify output as authoritative, a bad or injected result can trigger downstream actions. Because the pair is designed for orchestration and the blast radius can include irreversible actions, high is warranted.
conditions: IF Prefect uses Dify-produced outputs as inputs to automated tasks
IF no verification or approval step exists between the agents
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema checks on all outputs
Add human approval for destructive tasks
Log and diff intermediate artifacts
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between systems

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly handles conversation logs, knowledge base content, and model-provider API keys, while Prefect handles workflow metadata. If regulated data is placed into Dify and then propagated through Prefect, retention and residency policies can diverge. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Dify conversation logs or knowledge base files
IF Prefect retains workflow metadata longer than the source system
mitigations: Classify data before routing
Avoid placing regulated data in shared workflows
Set retention limits on both systems
Review residency settings for each deployment
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across systems
